# 9 Creative Ways to Promote Your Coworking Space with Content Marketing

Content marketing is a game-changer when promoting your coworking business in today's digital age. It's not just a buzzword but a powerful tool that can help you connect with your target audience and showcase what makes your space unique.

Here's a little stat to get you excited:

> Did you know 70% of people would learn about a company through articles instead of traditional advertisements? - [Source](https://searchengineland.com/what-is-content-marketing-388970#:~:text=70%25%20say%20they%20would%20prefer,awareness%20to%20consideration%20to%20decision.)

That's right! Content marketing allows you to tell your coworking story more authentically and engagingly.

And that's where this article comes in! We've compiled a fantastic list of 9 creative content marketing ideas to help you stand out and attract more members to your coworking space. So, dive into these innovative strategies to take your coworking business to new heights!

Let's get started!

## 1\. Know Your Target Audience

### Identifying the ideal customer profile for your coworking space

First things first – let's figure out who your dream members are! Think about the type of people who would love your coworking space. Are they freelancers, startups, remote workers, or creative professionals? Understanding your ideal customer profile will help you tailor your content to their needs and interests.

### Conducting market research to understand their preferences and pain points

Time to put on your detective hat! Dig deep into what makes your target audience tick. Check out their online behavior, social media, and what they discuss. Find out their pain points and challenges in their work life. This valuable info will guide you in creating content that addresses their needs.

### Creating content that resonates with the target audience

Now that you know your audience inside-out, it's time to create content that speaks their language! Offer valuable tips, insights, and solutions that make their workdays better. Be authentic, relatable, and let your coworking personality shine through your content.

_Remember, knowing your audience is like having a secret key to their hearts (and memberships)!_

## 2\. Showcase Your Space Through Visual Content

### High-quality photos and virtual tours of your coworking facility

Picture this: stunning photos that make people go "Wow!". Show off your coworking space with high-resolution images that capture its vibe and atmosphere. Remember to include virtual tours so potential members can explore every nook and cranny without leaving their couches!

### Creating captivating videos featuring the amenities and community

![An image of a person holding a camera and recording a video](https://res.cloudinary.com/kisi-kloud/image/upload/c_lfill,dpr_auto,e_vectorize:2:0,o_0,q_1,w_1880/v1/collections/cwr/blog/9-creative-ways-to-promote-your-space-with-content-marketing/johanna-buguet-W2D5bsAySEM-unsplash)

Lights, camera, action! Whip out your phone or camera and create awesome videos that show what separates your coworking space. Highlight the cool amenities, the buzzing community, and the exciting events. Let people experience the energy and camaraderie your space offers.

### Utilizing Instagram and Pinterest to share visual content

Say cheese, it's social media time! Instagram and Pinterest are the perfect platforms to flaunt your visual content. Post those jaw-dropping photos and engaging videos regularly. Use hashtags and geotags to reach a wider audience, and don't forget to interact with your followers – a little heart or comment can go a long way!

_Visual content is like a magic spell – it instantly draws people in and makes them want to be a part of your coworking wonderland._

## 3\. Engaging Blog Posts

### Writing informative blog posts about productivity, remote work, and collaboration

Share the knowledge! Whip up blog posts that offer practical tips and insights to help your target audience succeed in their work. Cover topics like boosting productivity, acing remote work, and mastering the art of collaboration. Be the go-to resource for all things coworking and professional growth.

### Highlighting success stories of businesses and individuals using your coworking space

Let the stars shine! Feature success stories of businesses and individuals who have thrived in your coworking space. Showcase their achievements, milestones, and how your space impacted their journey. People love inspiring stories. These success tales will make your coworking space irresistible.

### Collaborating with guest bloggers or industry influencers

Team up for success! Invite guest bloggers or industry influencers to share their expertise on your blog. Their unique perspectives will add fresh flavors to your content and attract new audiences. Plus, it's a win-win – you get exciting content, and they get exposure to your coworking community.

_Blog posts are like the heart of your content marketing strategy – they pump life and value into your coworking space._

## 4\. Host Webinars and Online Workshops

### Organizing webinars on coworking, entrepreneurship, and remote work

Get ready to go live! Host webinars that tackle hot topics in the coworking world. Discuss entrepreneurship tips, remote work best practices, and how coworking can boost productivity. These interactive sessions will engage your audience and position your space as a knowledge hub.

### Offering free workshops showcasing the benefits of coworking

![an image showing a diverse audience attending a workshop](https://res.cloudinary.com/kisi-kloud/image/upload/c_lfill,dpr_auto,e_vectorize:2:0,o_0,q_1,w_1880/v1/collections/cwr/blog/9-creative-ways-to-promote-your-space-with-content-marketing/sam-balye-w1FwDvIreZU-unsplash)

Knowledge is power, and you're the professor! Conduct free workshops that highlight the perks of coworking. Teach participants how shared workspaces foster creativity, collaboration, and business growth. Let them experience firsthand what your space has to offer.

### Promoting these events through email newsletters and social media

Spread the word like wildfire! Use email newsletters to announce upcoming webinars and workshops. Create eye-catching graphics and posts for social media platforms like Facebook, LinkedIn, and Twitter. Leverage the power of hashtags and encourage your community to share the event details with their networks.

Email marketing for coworking spaces

false

Coworking Influencer

# Email marketing for coworking spaces

[L Walker](https://www.coworks.com/blog/author/l-walker)

Nov 15, 2022

* * *

In previous conversations, Jake Bolling of CoworkingSEO.com has reviewed best practices and strategies for [optimizing your coworking space web site](https://blog.coworks.com/seo-basics-for-coworking-spaces) and for [marketing your coworking space using digital ads](https://blog.coworks.com/digital-advertising-for-coworking-spaces). Now, he wraps up his hat trick with email marketing.

“I want to focus on using email to nurture relationships,” Bolling said, “not just to sell. That’s an important distinction.” 

But first, a question. When was the last time you checked email? As long-in-the-tooth as email marketing might feel, it’s still one of the most effective marketing channels for any business, in particular for coworking spaces. 

“99% of email users check their inbox every single day, according to data from Optin Monster,” noted Bollling. “Some of them check it as many as 20 times a day and half of those people check it first thing in the morning. The majority of marketers are increasing their email engagement on a year to year basis. That's because the majority of people say that emails influence their purchase decisions.”

## Who should coworking spaces send email to?

“The legal answer is that you can email everybody who opts in to receive your communications,” Bolling said. “And that’s anyone who has interacted with you or your business, whether they had a tour, a day pass, attended an event, visited a member, been a past member, are local neighborhood business owners, etc.”

That opt-in list is your big bucket of contacts — your entire database. But the real art of email marketing comes from defining audiences or segments with that database.

## What kind of emails should coworking spaces send?

**Newsletters** sent on a regular basis that wrap up the week or month in your space, both what’s happened and what’s coming up.

**Event reminders** for specific networking opportunities, speaker presentations, or happy hours.

**Limited time promotions** such as Black Friday offers, new year’s discounts, referral opportunities, etc.

**Quick notifications** such as unexpected construction on local roads or WiFi disruptions during the workday.

**Auto responders** which are triggered by behaviors, such as booking a meeting room, scheduling a tour of the space, or renewing a membership. (Coworking spaces can even send texts as automated responses to missed phone calls — more on that later.)

**Sequences or workflows** are a set of emails that go out in a specific order, and are highly effective for onboarding new members or nurturing prospects. Coworks has an onboarding sequence here that you can customize and then CoworkingSEO.com has a proprietary sequence their clients get to use.

## Should coworking spaces send SMS texts?

Without a doubt, SMS texting in B2C is on the rise, and use cases are taking shape for how to be most effective over text as opposed to email. 

“95% of people read a text and respond within the first three minutes it's received,” Bolling cited. “According to SMS Comparison last year, 45% of clients responded to messages from brands that they follow.” 

But Bolling doesn’t see texts as a surrogate for email. Instead, it’s more about timeliness and brevity.

“Texts are more intrusive. So it is really important that you provide real value on a text message. I feel like the more intrusive you're going to be, the more value you need to deliver. You can do event reminders, urgent notices, missed payment notifications, and reservation reminders. I try to make everything seem personal, even when it's actually automated.” 

As mentioned above, tying text responses to missed calls is a powerful way to be responsive when a community manager only has so much time. Bolling and his team have automations as part of their services. And the Coworks platform includes push notifications to members through the [app](https://www.coworks.com/coworking-space-member-directory), but texting prospects is a very different kind of communication.

## Pay attention to who isn’t paying attention

Not everyone is going to love getting your emails, but they might not take the time to unsubscribe. That’s why it’s important to look at inactive contacts.

“If someone's not opening your emails after a few months, or even a year, take them off your list. It's probably doing you more harm than good.”

Having a big list isn’t helpful if only a small percentage of those contacts are actually engaged. You’re looking for high open rates and click through rates, not just size of a list. And one way to keep people engaged is to limit the number of emails you send each week. Bolling cited a Hubspot report that recommends no more than five emails in five business days.

## Use the right tools for email marketing of your coworking space

There are, of course, many email platforms to choose from, HubSpot and Mailchimp two of the most common. Segmenting, workflows, and testing are some of the most important features to look for. CoworkingSEO also offers a platform with email builder and logical sequences especially designed for coworking spaces.

However, you decide to leverage email marketing, do so with relationships in mind, sending the right message to the right person at the right time… and send an email you’d love to open!
